name: Practice (abhyāsa)
method_summary: Repeated effort to hold the mind in stability (1.13), cultivated for a long time, without interruption and with devotion — with austerity, celibacy, knowledge and faith — so that it becomes firmly grounded (1.14, YBh 1.14); it opens the stream of discrimination (YBh 1.12).
signs_of_progress: not quickly overpowered by the impressions of emergence (YBh 1.14)

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: Cultivating freedom from thirst for objects seen and heard of in scripture, by seeing their faults through reflection (1.15, YBh 1.15); higher dispassion, from discernment of the puruṣa, is freedom from thirst for the guṇas (1.16); dispassion even toward the highest powers yields kaivalya (3.50).
stage: all; higher dispassion for the advanced
signs_of_progress: the thought 'what was to be attained is attained ... the chain of becoming is cut' (YBh 1.16)

name: Devotion to Īśvara (īśvara-praṇidhāna)
method_summary: A special devotion (bhakti) to Īśvara, offering all actions to the supreme teacher or renouncing their fruit (YBh 1.23, 2.1; RM 1.23); Īśvara, won over, favours the yogin by mere intention and samādhi is near (1.23); a niyama and part of kriyā-yoga (2.1, 2.32).
signs_of_progress: realization of the inward consciousness and absence of obstacles (1.29); perfection of samādhi (2.45)

equivalents.note: Vyāsa defines praṇidhāna as a special bhakti; in Yoga its fruit is samādhi, not union with the Lord

name: Repetition of Oṃ with contemplation of Īśvara (praṇava-japa)
method_summary: Repeating the praṇava, Īśvara's designator, while contemplating its meaning, Īśvara (1.27–28, YBh 1.28); alternating self-study and yoga ('from self-study to yoga, from yoga to self-study').
signs_of_progress: one-pointed mind (YBh 1.28); inward consciousness realized, obstacles absent (1.29)

name: Practice on a single principle (ekatattva-abhyāsa)
method_summary: Holding the mind to one principle to counter the obstacles and their accompaniments (1.32, YBh 1.32).

name: Cultivating the four attitudes (maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā)
method_summary: Cultivating friendliness toward the happy, compassion toward the suffering, gladness toward the virtuous and equanimity toward the non-virtuous, so that white dharma arises and the mind becomes clear and steady (1.33, YBh 1.33); saṃyama on the first three gives strengths (3.23).
signs_of_progress: clarity of mind (citta-prasādana); strengths of friendliness etc. (3.23)

warnings.text: Equanimity toward the wicked is not a cultivation; no samādhi and no strength come from it.

equivalents.note: Same four attitudes and 'vihāra' vocabulary (YBh 4.10) as the Buddhist brahmavihāras; objects and aim differ (YS 1.33 assigns each to a class of object)

name: Expulsion and retention of breath (1.34)
method_summary: Steadying the mind by expelling the air of the abdomen through the nostrils with a special effort and by holding it (1.34, YBh 1.34). Summary only.
notes: No measures are given in the YS; haṭha texts add warnings about breath practice (units U28/U29).

name: Concentration giving rise to subtle sense-perception (1.35)
method_summary: Concentrating on the tip of the nose, tip, middle and root of the tongue, or the palate, until divine smell, taste, touch, sound or form is perceived; such experiences bind the mind to steadiness and confirm what scripture and the teacher say (YBh 1.35).
signs_of_progress: awareness of divine smell, taste, form, touch or sound (YBh 1.35)

name: The sorrowless, luminous activity (1.36)
method_summary: Concentrating on the lotus of the heart until the luminous buddhi appears like the light of sun, moon, planets and gems; or absorbing the mind in I-am-ness until it is calm and endless like a waveless ocean (YBh 1.36).
signs_of_progress: luminous appearances; 'I am' alone (YBh 1.36)

name: Mind on one free of passion (1.37)
method_summary: Letting the mind take as its support the mind of one free of passion (1.37, YBh 1.37).

name: Support in the knowledge of dream and sleep (1.38)
method_summary: Letting the mind rest on the knowledge of dream or of sleep as its support, taking that form (1.38, YBh 1.38).

name: Meditation on whatever is agreeable (1.39)
method_summary: Meditating on whatever object one finds agreeable; the mind stable there becomes stable elsewhere too (1.39, YBh 1.39).
signs_of_progress: mastery from the smallest to the greatest (1.40)

name: Kriyā-yoga (austerity, self-study, devotion to Īśvara)
method_summary: For the unconcentrated mind: austerity, self-study and devotion to Īśvara together (2.1), to cultivate samādhi and thin the afflictions (2.2); the yogin should first be intent on it (RM 2.1).
signs_of_progress: afflictions thinned, like seeds burnt (YBh 2.2)

warnings.text: Austerity is to be practised so as not to disturb the clarity of the mind.

name: Austerity (tapas)
method_summary: Bearing the pairs of opposites — hunger and thirst, cold and heat, standing and sitting, silence — with vows as suitable (YBh 2.32); it breaks up impurity, without which yoga does not succeed (YBh 2.1). Summary only: the fasting vows the bhāṣya names (kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, sāntapana) are not described here.
signs_of_progress: perfection of body and senses through the destruction of impurity (2.43)

warnings.text: It should be practised so as not to disturb the clarity of the mind (tac ca cittaprasādanam abādhamānam anenāsevyam).

notes: Marked restricted because it includes prolonged fasting vows; summary and the text's own warning only.

name: Self-study (svādhyāya)
method_summary: Repetition of the praṇava and other purifying formulas, or study of scriptures on liberation (YBh 2.1, 2.32); repetition of mantras preceded by the praṇava (RM 2.1).
signs_of_progress: contact with the chosen deity; gods, sages and siddhas appear (2.44, YBh 2.44)

name: The restraints (yama)
method_summary: Keeping non-harming, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy and non-possessiveness (2.30), without limitation of class, place, time or occasion — the great vow (2.31); non-harming is the root of all (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: the fruits of 2.35–39

name: Non-harming (ahiṃsā)
method_summary: Not injuring any being in any way at any time (YBh 2.30), kept as a great vow (2.31).
signs_of_progress: hostility abandoned in one's presence (2.35)

name: Truthfulness (satya)
method_summary: Speech and mind according to fact, spoken for the good of all beings after examination (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: actions and their fruits rest on one's word (2.36)

warnings.text: Truth spoken to harm beings is not truth but sin, a semblance of merit leading to painful darkness.

name: Non-stealing (asteya)
method_summary: Freedom from desire for what is not one's own (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: all jewels present themselves (2.37)

name: Celibacy (brahmacarya)
method_summary: Restraint of the generative organ with the senses guarded (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: vigour gained; the siddha can impart knowledge to disciples (2.38, YBh 2.38)

name: Non-possessiveness (aparigraha)
method_summary: Not appropriating objects, seeing the faults of acquiring, keeping, losing, attachment and harm (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: knowledge of the how of births: 'Who was I? How was I?' (2.39, YBh 2.39)

name: The observances (niyama)
method_summary: Purity, contentment, austerity, self-study and devotion to Īśvara (2.32, YBh 2.32).
signs_of_progress: the fruits of 2.40–45

name: Purity (śauca)
method_summary: Outer purity with earth, water and pure food, and inner washing away of the mind's stains (YBh 2.32).
signs_of_progress: disgust for one's own body, non-contact with others; purity of sattva, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery of the senses, fitness to see the self (2.40–41)

name: Contentment (saṃtoṣa)
method_summary: Not wanting more than the means at hand (YBh 2.32).
signs_of_progress: unsurpassed happiness (2.42)

name: Cultivating the opposite (pratipakṣa-bhāvanā)
method_summary: When harmful thoughts arise, reflect on their opposites: that violence and the rest, done, caused or approved, from greed, anger or delusion, mild to intense, bear endless suffering and ignorance; that having taken refuge in yoga by granting fearlessness to all beings, to take such thoughts up again is to be like a dog eating its vomit (2.33–34, YBh 2.33–34).

warnings.text: Harmful thoughts have endless suffering and ignorance as their fruit.

name: Posture (āsana)
method_summary: A steady and comfortable seat (2.46), achieved by relaxing effort and by coalescence with the endless (2.47); Vyāsa lists padmāsana, bhadrāsana, svastika, daṇḍāsana, sitting with a support, paryaṅka, the curlew, elephant and camel seats, the even configuration, and 'as is comfortable' (YBh 2.46).
signs_of_progress: the limbs do not tremble (YBh 2.47); no assault by the pairs of opposites (2.48)
notes: Vīrāsana appears in some editions' list of YBh 2.46.

name: Breath-regulation (prāṇāyāma)
method_summary: With posture mastered, cutting off the movement of inhalation and exhalation (2.49): external, internal or suspended, observed by place, time and number, becoming long and subtle (2.50, YBh 2.50). Summary only; no measures or counts.
signs_of_progress: the covering of the light dwindles (2.52); the mind becomes fit for concentration (2.53)
notes: YBh 2.52 quotes: 'There is no austerity higher than prāṇāyāma.' Haṭha texts add warnings (U28/U29).

name: The fourth prāṇāyāma (2.51)
method_summary: A breath-stilling that goes beyond the external and internal spheres, reached gradually after mastering the stages (2.51, YBh 2.51). Summary only.
notes: Marked restricted as a form of breath suspension; no method given.

name: Sense-withdrawal (pratyāhāra)
method_summary: The senses, disjoined from their objects, follow the stilled mind as bees follow the queen bee (2.54, YBh 2.54).
signs_of_progress: supreme mastery of the senses (2.55)

name: Concentration (dhāraṇā)
method_summary: Binding the mind to one place — navel wheel, heart-lotus, light in the head, tip of the nose or tongue, or an external object (3.1, YBh 3.1).

name: Meditation (dhyāna)
method_summary: The continuous flow of a single cognition on the place of concentration (3.2); it removes the gross activities of the afflictions (2.11).

name: Samādhi as the eighth limb
method_summary: Meditation shining only as its object, as if empty of its own form (3.3, YBh 3.3).

name: Saṃyama
method_summary: Concentration, meditation and samādhi together on one object (3.4), applied stage by stage (3.6) to objects such as the three transformations, the sun, moon, pole star, navel wheel, throat-well, heart, the moment and its sequence (3.16–52).
signs_of_progress: the light of insight (3.5); the powers (3.16–49)

warnings.text: The powers are obstacles in samādhi; they are powers only in the emergent state.
Invited by the celestials, form neither attachment nor pride, for the undesired would recur.
Without mastering the lower stage one does not gain saṃyama on higher stages by skipping.

name: Cultivating discriminative discernment (viveka-khyāti)
method_summary: Cultivating the cognition of the difference between sattva and puruṣa until it is unwavering, false knowledge burnt like a seed (2.26, YBh 2.26); the practice of the limbs makes knowledge shine up to it (2.28).
signs_of_progress: the sevenfold final insight (2.27); the mind bends toward kaivalya (4.26)

warnings.text: In its gaps other cognitions ('I am', 'mine') arise from impressions; they are removed like the afflictions.
